alternativeSelection.assessment: studies signals, feedback, computational models and electricity systems through mathematics, robotics and renewable energy design. Neuroscience and signal analysis support interests in medical electronics but leave out the design and testing of the devices themselves. Delft also requires circuit design, electromagnetism, semiconductor devices and integrated electrical engineering projects.

audience.programmeDescription: Students combine mathematics and physics with circuits, signals, digital systems, telecommunications and electrical energy. Projects develop skills in system design and experimentation before a minor and graduation project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR combination studies signals, feedback, computational models and electricity systems through mathematics, robotics and renewable energy design. Delft also requires circuit design, electromagnetism, semiconductor devices and integrated electrical engineering projects.

curriculum.limitation: The 30-EC minor remains open, subject to approval and overlap rules. Two distinct 5-EC electives are selected across years two and three. The 15-EC graduation project requires completion of all first- and second-year courses.
